clues.explanation: Band-Aid is literally a cover for wounds — and it's found in medicine cabinets from Tokyo to Topeka. The most helpful cover-up in history.
Mom kisses the boo-boo first, then smooths one on. The original two-step first aid protocol. Clinically proven to make it feel better.
You cannot stick one of these on hurt feelings. It is only rated for physical wounds. Trust us, people have tried the other way.
The wound that earned it hurts. But honestly? Ripping it off a week later hurts more. Two pains for the price of one.

clues.text: YOU STICK WITH THEM 'CAUSE THEY'RE STUCK ON YOU
clues.explanation: The adhesive side is extremely committed. It will stick with you through thick and thin — and through arm hair, which is the real test of loyalty.
Between the pipe and deducing a man's entire backstory from cigar ash, this fellow detected more from smoke than a fire alarm ever could. Elementary.

clues.text: A MAN WITH MANY BRIEF CASES
clues.explanation: Cases that are brief AND the kind you carry. This man lived for a good double meaning — which is ironic, since he was famously literal about everything else.

clues.text: JUST LIKE YOU, HE LOVES A GOOD CLUE
clues.explanation: His entire career was built on them. He followed them, catalogued them, and built a whole deductive method around them. And here you are, doing the same. Great minds.

clues.text: SCHOOLS HIS DEAR SIDEKICK IN THE WAYS OF INVESTIGATION
clues.explanation: Poor Watson gets a full deductive reasoning lecture every single time. 'Elementary, my dear Watson' was basically 'let me explain this very slowly, again.'

clues.text: FICTIONAL BRITISH SLEUTH WHO ALWAYS FINDS THE TRUTH
clues.explanation: 221B Baker Street. Pipe. Deerstalker. Never actually said 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in the original books, but we forgive him. The one and only.
Invented in 1904 — Ohio and Pennsylvania are still arguing about who did it first. Either way, America has claimed this dessert for over 120 years and is not letting go.
Order it fast. The ice cream has no patience for slow eaters and the banana itself goes from firm to soft on you. It is a dessert with a timeline.
The long oval dish it's served in is called a boat. Or maybe the banana itself splits open like a hull. Either way, this dessert is a vessel — for joy, mostly.
The banana comes with a peel. The dessert has appeal. One letter makes all the difference, and this clue is not sorry about it for even one second.

clues.text: PEOPLE GO NUTS FOR ITS 3 SCOOPS
clues.explanation: Chocolate, vanilla, and strawberry. Plus whipped cream. Plus the cherry on top. Plus — and this is the kicker — actual nuts. The clue was being literal the whole time.
Manhattan and Staten Island say hello. New York City is literally built on islands and surrounded by water — yet somehow still the most landlocked-feeling place on Earth, traffic-wise.
The City That Never Sleeps. It's a point of pride, not a diagnosis. The real estate market and the 24-hour deli scene are both equally responsible.

clues.text: THAT IS ONE GIANT PIECE OF FRUIT
clues.explanation: The Big Apple. Nobody is 100% sure how the nickname started, but jazz musicians, horse racing, and a 1970s tourism campaign all had a hand in it. The apple itself had nothing to do with it.

clues.text: DESPITE ITS NAME, IT'S OVER 200 YEARS OLD
clues.explanation: 'New' York was founded as New Amsterdam in 1624 and renamed in 1664. Four centuries old and still calling itself new. The audacity. The confidence. Iconic.

clues.text: IT'S SO NICE THEY NAMED IT TWICE
clues.explanation: New York, New York. The state AND the city share the name. Frank Sinatra made a whole song about it. If you can make it there, you can make it anywhere — and apparently say the city name at least twice while doing so.
